title: Regression Watchtower: p95/p99 telemetry and dashboard matrix by endpoint/model/region
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Build a resilient, sliceable dashboard and automated regression watcher that surfaces p95/p99 latency regressions and tokens/sec anomalies across endpoint (route), model, and region. This ticket ties synthetic-load harness runs into the telemetry pipeline and adds deterministic alerting thresholds, a playback-based root-cause drilldown, and a retention policy for quantile rollups.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New dashboard with matrix view that can toggle dimensions: route, model, model-variant, region, and traffic-shape (prod vs synthetic). Panels show p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, 95->99 delta, and request volume.
A2: Automated regression watcher that evaluates daily quantile rollups and emits incidents when p95 or p99 increase beyond relative or absolute thresholds (configurable by route/model/region).
A3: Integration with existing synthetic load harness so scheduled runs produce labeled telemetry (load-id, seed, kernel-mode) and are discoverable in the dashboard and alerts.
A4: Playbook links and a drilldown workflow from alert -> synthetic replay -> tail-trace -> kernel/runtime assignment are documented in the runbook.
A5: Dashboards respect data retention and rollup policies; raw request traces kept for 14d, quantile rollups retained 90d for historical diffing.
A6: Regression smoke-tests (CI job) that inject synthetic regression and verify the watcher fires and a dashboard panel updates accordingly.
technical_notes: Telemetry source: augment percentile emitter to attach 'test_run_id' when flagged by harness; ensure streaming backfill path annotates historical synthetic runs.
Quantile storage: create a new rollup key format 'route|model|region|variant|hour' so matrix queries are efficient and cardinality is bounded.
Alerting logic: two-mode thresholds — relative (e.g., p95 increases >20% vs 7d baseline) and absolute (e.g., p99 > 1.2s). Allow per-entity overrides via config store.
Visualization: implement matrix in dashboard backend using pre-aggregated rollups and a fast diff endpoint that returns N worst regressions for auto-highlighting.
Sampling: for high-volume routes, sample traces for tail attribution at adjustable rates to avoid observability cost explosion; rely on KV-cache indicators in trace to pinpoint kernel paths.
Backfill: migration job to compute 90d rollups from raw events for existing endpoints; schedule as low-priority offline job to not impact ingestion cluster.
Security: dashboards use existing Console RBAC; ensure private deployments (Private) use configured log sinks so retained telemetry is tenant-isolated.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Schema and rollup key work (2d) — update quantile emitter + storage schema and migration job.
Step 2: Synthetic harness tagging (1d) — add test_run_id propagation to telemetry and harness launcher.
Step 3: Dashboard backend endpoints (3d) — matrix query + diff endpoint + worst-regressions API.
Step 4: Dashboard front-end (3d) — matrix with filters, heatmap, per-cell drilldown to traces and synthetic run details.
Step 5: Regression watcher (2d) — scheduled job + alerting integration + per-entity configs.
Step 6: CI smoke-tests and runbook updates (1d).
Estimated total: 12 engineering days (parallelize tasks across telemetry and console owners).
testing_plan: Unit tests for rollup key generation and migration job.
End-to-end test: synthetic harness run -> telemetry ingestion -> rollup -> dashboard visible within SLA (<= 15m).
Regression injection test: artificially inflate latency in a canary model to verify watcher alerts and dashboard highlighting.
Load test: execute scheduled synthetic runs at production-like qps to validate storage costs and sampling heuristics.
Manual UAT with PM and SRE to validate runbook and incident flow.
Create CI job that runs the smoke regression and asserts alert received in PagerDuty channel (test-only route).
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Backend + emitter changes deployed behind feature flag; run migration with low parallelism.
Stage 2: Enable dashboard read-only for internal users; collect feedback for two weekdays.
Stage 3: Enable regression watcher in dry-run mode (alerts logged to monitoring but not page) for 72h.
Stage 4: Flip watcher to active for a small set of critical routes (alpha customers) and monitor false positives.
Stage 5: Full rollout to all routes and add automated synthetic schedule for daily runs per region.
Rollback: disable feature flag and revert to previous rollup reader.
